posts.text: 🚨 LinkedIn Breaking News: The Only 2 Types of People on My Feed 🚨

Everyone is asking:
"Will AI agents replace my job?"

Wrong question entirely.

Here is the right one.
And the honest answer to it 👇

The wrong question creates fear.
The right question creates strategy.

The wrong question: "Will AI agents replace me?"
The right question: "Which parts of my role
are agent-ready and which are not?"

Let me break this down properly.

AGENT-READY TASKS:
(AI agents can handle these now)

→ Repetitive data processing
→ Scheduled report generation
→ Standard email responses
→ Calendar management
→ Basic research and summarizing
→ Social media scheduling
→ Invoice and payment follow up
→ Lead qualification scoring
→ Meeting transcription and notes
→ Document formatting and filing

HUMAN-ESSENTIAL TASKS:
(AI agents cannot do these meaningfully)

→ Building genuine trust with clients
→ Reading a room in a negotiation
→ Making judgment calls with incomplete data
→ Creative problem solving with real stakes
→ Mentoring and developing people
→ Building organizational culture
→ Ethical decision making
→ Managing complex human conflict
→ Genuine empathy in difficult situations
→ Strategic vision from lived experience

NOW HERE IS THE CRITICAL INSIGHT:

Look at both lists carefully.

The agent-ready list?
Most professionals spend
40 to 60 percent of their day on it.

The human-essential list?
Most professionals wish they
could spend 80 percent of their day on it.

AI agents are not taking what you love.

They are taking what you tolerate.

The professionals who understand this
will use AI agents to eliminate
the tolerated work from their days.

And spend those recovered hours
on the work only humans can do.

The professionals who fear this?

Will spend the next 3 years
doing the tolerated work manually.

While their colleagues
who automated it are doing
more meaningful work.
Faster. Better. With more energy.

The replacement fear is real.
But the thing most people are afraid
of losing is usually the thing
they would be happy to let go.

Which tasks on the agent-ready list
are you currently spending
the most time on?

Be honest. Comment below 👇
#AIAgents #FutureOfWork #AIAutomation #JobsAndAI #HumanSkills

Most people are building AI automations.

The smartest people are building
multi-agent systems.

Here is the difference.
And why it matters right now 👇

ONE AI AGENT doing everything:

Like hiring one brilliant person
and asking them to simultaneously
research, write, design,
review, approve and publish.

The output gets worse.
Because even brilliant people
lose quality when context switching constantly.

AI agents have the same problem.
One agent handling everything
produces mediocre output on everything.

MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM:

Multiple specialized agents.
Each doing one thing.
Extremely well.

Then coordinating automatically.

Here is a real example I built:

MY CONTENT MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM:

AGENT 1: The Researcher
Specialization: Finding information
Tools given: Web search, Perplexity
Task: Research topic deeply.
Return structured findings only.

AGENT 2: The Writer
Specialization: Creating content
Tools given: ChatGPT with custom instructions
Task: Take research. Write post draft.
Match my tone and style exactly.

AGENT 3: The Editor
Specialization: Quality checking
Tools given: Claude
Task: Review draft. Check for:
→ Clarity issues
→ Claims needing verification
→ Tone inconsistencies
→ Missing context
Return edited version plus feedback.

AGENT 4: The Publisher
Specialization: Scheduling and posting
Tools given: Buffer, LinkedIn API
Task: Take approved content.
Schedule at optimal time.
Post automatically.

THE COORDINATION LAYER:
Make.com orchestrates all four agents.
Output of Agent 1 triggers Agent 2.
Output of Agent 2 triggers Agent 3.
Approved output triggers Agent 4.

WHAT THIS PRODUCES:

Research quality: Specialist level
Writing quality: Consistent voice
Editorial quality: Errors caught
Publishing: Zero manual work

All four happening simultaneously
on different pieces of content.

Like having a four person content team
that works 24 hours a day.

THE HONEST BUILD TIME:

This took me 3 weeks to build properly.
Multiple failures along the way.
Not beginner territory.

But the output quality?

Significantly better than
one agent trying to do everything.

The future of AI automation
is not smarter single agents.

It is well designed teams of agents.
Each specialized. Each excellent.
Coordinated intelligently.

Are you still using single agents?
Or have you started experimenting
with multi-agent approaches?

Tell me what you are building 👇
#MultiAgentAI #AIAgents #AIAutomation #AgentArchitecture #AdvancedAI

Google just launched Agentspace
inside Google Workspace.

If your company uses Gmail,
Google Docs or Google Drive
this changes how you work.
Starting now.

Here is the complete breakdown 👇

WHAT GOOGLE AGENTSPACE ACTUALLY IS:

Not a chatbot inside Google.
Not a smarter search.

An AI agent that works across
your entire Google Workspace
and connects to external tools.

It has access to:
→ All your Gmail conversations
→ All your Google Drive documents
→ All your Google Calendar events
→ All your Google Meet recordings
→ Your connected business tools

And it uses all of that context
to help you work differently.

WHAT IT CAN DO RIGHT NOW:

CAPABILITY 1: NotebookLM Integration
Upload any document.
The agent becomes an expert on it.
Ask it questions about your own
company documents, policies, reports.
Get cited answers with sources.

CAPABILITY 2: Research Agent
Give it a research goal.
It searches the web.
It searches your internal documents.
It synthesizes both.
Returns a comprehensive brief.

CAPABILITY 3: Meeting Intelligence
Connects to Google Meet recordings.
Transcribes automatically.
Extracts action items.
Identifies decisions made.
Creates follow up tasks.

CAPABILITY 4: Cross-App Workflows
"Summarize all emails from
this client this month and
create a briefing document in Drive"
It does this across apps automatically.

CAPABILITY 5: Custom Agents
Build specialized agents
for specific business functions.
HR agent. Legal agent.
Finance agent. Sales agent.
Each trained on relevant documents.

THE HONEST LIMITATIONS:

→ Currently in early access
→ Enterprise pricing not beginner friendly
→ Requires Google Workspace Business plan
→ Custom agents need IT involvement
→ Data privacy settings critical to review

THE BIG PICTURE:

Microsoft has Copilot in Office 365.
Google has Agentspace in Workspace.
Salesforce has Agentforce in CRM.

Every platform you use for work
is becoming an AI agent platform.

The tools are not changing.
The intelligence inside them is.

And the professionals who learn
to direct these agents effectively?

They will produce what used to take
a full team.
With the quality of a specialist.
In the time of an individual.

Is your company using
Google Workspace or Microsoft 365?

And have they started
exploring AI agents yet?

Tell me where your organization
is in this journey 👇
#GoogleAgentspace #AIAgents #GoogleWorkspace #WorkplaceAI #AIAutomation

I asked 5 different AI agents
to do the same task.

Same instruction.
Same goal.
Very different results.

Here is the honest comparison
nobody has done yet 👇

THE TASK I GAVE ALL FIVE:

"Research the top 3 competitors
of a LinkedIn automation tool.
Find their pricing.
Identify their main weaknesses
based on public reviews.
Create a simple comparison summary."

A real research task.
Something a junior analyst
would spend 3 hours on.

Here is what each agent did:

AGENT 1: ChatGPT with browsing
Time taken: 4 minutes 30 seconds
Quality of research: Good
Pricing accuracy: Mostly current
Weakness analysis: Surface level
Format of output: Well structured
Overall: Reliable but not deep

AGENT 2: Claude with Computer Use
Time taken: 7 minutes 20 seconds
Quality of research: Excellent
Pricing accuracy: Very current
Weakness analysis: Detailed and nuanced
Format of output: Comprehensive
Overall: Best quality. Slowest speed.

AGENT 3: Perplexity AI
Time taken: 45 seconds
Quality of research: Good for facts
Pricing accuracy: Current
Weakness analysis: Limited
Format of output: Clean summary
Overall: Fastest. Less analytical depth.

AGENT 4: Zapier AI Agent
Time taken: 3 minutes
Quality of research: Moderate
Pricing accuracy: Acceptable
Weakness analysis: Template feeling
Format of output: Structured nicely
Overall: Good for connected workflows.
Less strong as standalone researcher.

AGENT 5: Google Gemini Advanced
Time taken: 2 minutes 10 seconds
Quality of research: Very good
Pricing accuracy: Current
Weakness analysis: Good
Format of output: Clean and readable
Overall: Underrated. Strong performer.

THE HONEST VERDICT:

For pure research quality: Claude wins
For speed: Perplexity wins
For connected workflows: Zapier Agent wins
For balance of both: Gemini surprises
For reliability and trust: ChatGPT wins

THE PATTERN I NOTICED:

No single agent dominates everything.

The professionals winning with AI agents
are not using the best one.

They are using the right one
for each specific task.

That is the real skill.
Not which tool you use.
But knowing which tool
for which job.

Which of these agents are you
currently using for research tasks?

And what do you use it for specifically?

Comment below 👇
#AIAgents #ChatGPT #Claude #Perplexity #AIComparison
